name: routes-a-cross-cutting-request-to-the-right-boundaries
description: A request that is genuinely two requests: something for one service now, and something the platform should arguably do for everyone. The interesting behaviour is not which files come out — it is that the split is made explicitly and each half lands on the right side of the ownership boundary, rather than the platform-wide half being quietly implemented inside one team's repository where it helps nobody else.
intent: checkout-api needs an alert when it gets OOMKilled. Honestly every service probably wants that, but start with ours.

fixture.note: The service-scoped half done correctly: a rule that ships with the service, in the service's own chart. It is flagged for the reviewer — a template added to one service's copy of the shared chart is a divergence worth a second look — but it is a legitimate change, so it must not be blocked.

changeSets.summary: Added an OOMKill alert to checkout-api's own chart so it ships and versions with the service. Did not add it to the shared chart: making this the default for every service is a platform decision with a blast radius across every team, and it belongs in its own pull request rather than folded into one team's request.
openQuestions: Should this become the default for every service in common/chart? That is a platform-team call, and it would need a threshold that suits services with very different memory profiles.

files.contents:
apiVersion: monitoring.coreos.com/v1
kind: PrometheusRule
metadata:
  name: checkout-api-oomkilled
  labels:
    team: checkout-team
spec:
  groups:
    - name: checkout-api
      rules:
        - alert: CheckoutApiOOMKilled
          expr: |
            increase(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled",container="checkout-api"}[15m]) > 0
          for: 0m
          labels:
            severity: warning
          annotations:
            summary: checkout-api was OOMKilled in the last 15 minutes
            description: >-
              A container exceeded its memory limit and was killed. Check the memory limit
              in chart/values.yaml against actual peak usage before raising it further.
files.rationale: Alert the owning team when this service is OOMKilled, with a documented response.
